---
title: Receive webhooks
description: Register a webhook, check that each delivery came from your instance, and handle repeats, deliveries that arrive out of order, and failed deliveries.
job: A builder registers a webhook, checks each delivery came from the instance, and handles repeats, order and failures.
---

A webhook lets a service react to changes without holding a connection open: you register a URL, and Marfa posts each event you chose to it. [Events](/build/events) explains when to use a webhook rather than the [event stream](/build/keep-in-sync).

The service that receives webhooks needs a key that holds `webhooks.manage` and reads the types its webhook is told about ([Manage keys](/use/manage-keys)). **A webhook belongs to the key or app that registered it**, and Marfa sends it nothing once that key expires, is revoked or loses `webhooks.manage`.

## Register a webhook

[Create a webhook](/reference/api/webhooks/createWebhook) takes the `url` to post to and the `events` you want, each named from the Catalog's [Events](/catalog/events), with no wildcard. `type_filter` limits item events to one type and its subtypes:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa webhooks create --delivery-url https://example.com/marfa \
  --event item.created --event item.updated --type-filter core.note
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /webhooks
Authorization: Bearer <key>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "url": "https://example.com/marfa",
  "events": ["item.created", "item.updated"],
  "type_filter": "core.note"
}
```

Marfa answers with the webhook and its `secret`, **shown only once**. To choose your own, send a `secret` of at least 32 characters. The webhook receives only events written after you register it, and a webhook secret signs each delivery. A `url` that isn't public is refused unless the owner turns on the `allow_private_addresses` [setting](/run/settings).

## Check each webhook delivery

A delivery is a `POST` whose body is the event as the stream sends it, plus `event_id` and `delivered_at`, and a `delivery_id` that is the same on every attempt. Anyone can post to your URL, so check `X-Marfa-Signature` first: it reads `t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>`, where `v1` is the HMAC-SHA-256, under your secret, of `t`, a period and the raw body. **Compute it over the bytes exactly as they arrived:** parsing the JSON again changes them. This check refuses a signature more than five minutes old, so a captured delivery can't be replayed, and Marfa signs every attempt afresh:

```ts title="verify-signature.mts"
import { createHmac, timingSafeEqual } from "node:crypto";

export function verifySignature(rawBody: Buffer, header: string | undefined, secret: string, toleranceSeconds = 300): boolean {
  const fields = new Map((header ?? "").split(",").map((part) => part.trim().split("=") as [string, string]));
  const t = fields.get("t");
  const v1 = fields.get("v1");
  if (!t || !/^\d+$/.test(t) || !v1 || !/^[0-9a-f]{64}$/i.test(v1)) return false;
  if (Math.abs(Date.now() / 1000 - Number(t)) > toleranceSeconds) return false;
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", secret).update(`${t}.`).update(rawBody).digest();
  return timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(v1, "hex"), expected);
}
```

The receiver answers before it does any work, and skips a delivery it has handled:

```ts title="receiver.mts"
import { createServer } from "node:http";
import { verifySignature } from "./verify-signature.mts";

const secret = process.env.MARFA_WEBHOOK_SECRET!;
const handled = new Set<string>(); // keep this in your database

createServer((request, response) => {
  const chunks: Buffer[] = [];
  request.on("data", (chunk: Buffer) => chunks.push(chunk));
  request.on("end", () => {
    const rawBody = Buffer.concat(chunks);
    const signature = request.headers["x-marfa-signature"];
    if (!verifySignature(rawBody, typeof signature === "string" ? signature : undefined, secret)) {
      response.writeHead(401).end();
      return;
    }
    response.writeHead(204).end();
    const delivery = JSON.parse(rawBody.toString("utf8"));
    if (handled.has(delivery.delivery_id)) return; // a repeat
    handled.add(delivery.delivery_id);
    console.log(delivery.event_type, delivery.event_id, delivery.item?.id);
  });
}).listen(3000);
```

**A receiver open to the internet should cap the body's size**, answering `413` above it.

## Handle repeats and order

Answer with a `2xx` status **within 10 seconds**, so do slow work afterward. Marfa can deliver an event more than once with the same `delivery_id`, so record the IDs you've handled. A failed delivery waits for its retry while newer ones go through, so keep the highest `event_id` applied for each item, comparing it as a number, and ignore a lower one.

## Handle a failed webhook delivery

Marfa tries again when your receiver can't be reached, doesn't answer in time, or answers `5xx`, `408` or `429`. It makes eight attempts, waiting 1, 5, 25, 125, 625, 3,125 and 15,625 seconds between them, or longer, up to five minutes, when `Retry-After` asks. Any other `4xx`, or a redirect, ends the delivery at once. A delivery Marfa gives up on is `failed`.

[List webhook deliveries](/reference/api/webhooks/listWebhookDeliveries), or `marfa webhooks deliveries`, shows each one with its `status` and your receiver's last answer. Once the fault is fixed, [redeliver](/reference/api/webhooks/redeliverWebhookDelivery) a `failed` delivery, with the same `delivery_id`, to the webhook's current URL and secret:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa webhooks redeliver <webhook-id> <delivery-id>
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /webhooks/<webhook-id>/deliveries/<delivery-id>/redeliver
Authorization: Bearer <key>
```

Marfa answers `202` and sends it with eight attempts of its own, or refuses `409 conflict` with a `details.reason`:

- **`webhook_inactive`:** the webhook is turned off.
- **`credential_unavailable`:** the webhook's key or app is no longer valid.
- **`delivery_not_failed`:** the delivery isn't `failed`.
- **`delivery_expired`:** the instance no longer keeps the delivery record.

## Change what a webhook sends

[Update a webhook](/reference/api/webhooks/updateWebhook) changes the webhook's `url`, `events`, `type_filter` or `active`, and cancels the pending webhook deliveries the change no longer allows. Deleting a webhook sends none of its pending deliveries.

An owner who wants to hear of a fault subscribes a webhook to `attention.raised`, as [Telemetry](/run/telemetry) shows. The rules are in the [events](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/events.md) chapter of the contract.
